I quite like this game actually, and I think they found the perfect balance between interesting city builder and punishing resource management / survival schemes. As far as population management goes, pay attention to the maximum occupancies of houses, as most of them have different values for how many people fit when starting a new family versus how many fit when re-homing an existing family (house destroyed in natural disaster or manually removed). As far as nomads go, I've had bringing them in screw long term villages so many times... I have a tendency to overbuild and stretch my workers pretty thin, which can work well in the early game, but is not viable long term. I often find myself wanting to bring in nomads to beef up my worker population, only to have them not do much actual work and then encounter a food shortage.

If you're interested in mods, Colonial Charter is fairly all inclusive, and I find it makes the game feel more complete. It adds a variety of different positions and production chains, allowing the game to have more of a "late game" feel to it.
